title: A Wolf for the Veil
premise: Odile Villalobos has spent her life in the Veiled Valley, the one place where the old magic cannot reach — and where her oath-bound gift of swordspeaking lies dormant. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into her hands, she is dragged beyond the valley's edge into a kingdom ruled by a king slowly being devoured by the thing wearing his crown. Guided by a disgraced hedge-witch and a deserter who once served the crown, Odile must unbind the king before the coronation of the crown-thing's chosen heir. In the end she learns the valley was built to hide her lineage: she is the last heir of the swordspeaker oaths, and she breaks the binding not with steel but by speaking her own true name — choosing found family over bloodline and claiming a home she builds rather than inherits.
about_author: Ansel Lockridge is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade drawing borders for governments before turning to stories about people who refuse them. They live in a drafty house full of half-finished maps and write about belonging in worlds that keep trying to assign it.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: POV Odile. On the eve of the valley's founding festival, Odile tends her late mother's forge and practices sword-forms that hum with words she doesn't understand. A stranger collapses at the treeline, bleeding from wounds no blade made. She takes him in against village law. Emotional beat: restless longing beneath a life that fits too well.

chapters.title: A Map Pressed Into Unwilling Hands
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The dying courier, Merric, gives her a map inked in blood and a warning: the king is being eaten from inside. Village elders demand the map be burned; when they try to take it, the valley itself shudders — magic testing its walls. Merric dies at dawn. Emotional beat: guilt and the first crack in everything she trusted.

chapters.title: Out past the Edge of the World
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Exiled or fleeing — even she isn't sure which — Odile crosses the valley boundary and feels her dormant gift wake like a second heartbeat. The outside world is louder, stranger, and watched. She is ambushed by crown riders hunting the map. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration tangled together; identity beginning to shift.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Odile, with a brief interlude from Sera the hedge-witch. Rescued from the riders by Sera, an exiled witch who recognizes the map as a route to the king's binding-circles, Odile strikes a wary bargain: guide her to the capital, and Sera will teach her what the swordspeaker oaths are. Emotional beat: distrust slowly becoming alliance.

chapters.title: The Deserter's Road
chapters.summary: POV Tam, the deserter. A former royal guard who fled after seeing what sits behind the king's eyes, Tam joins them on the road, haunted and sardonic. Through his memories we see the court's rot: ministers replaced, laughter gone wrong. An ambush by the crown-thing's hounds forces the three to fight as one. Emotional beat: shared survival forging fragile trust.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Reaching the capital in disguise, they witness the king in public — and Odile's swordspeech flares involuntarily, answering the thing in him. It notices her. That night, an invitation arrives bearing the royal seal: the king requests an audience. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve; she stops running.

chapters.title: Audience with a Hollow King
chapters.summary: POV Odile. In the throne room, the king surfaces for moments between the crown-thing's grip, begging Odile to end it — but killing him feeds the thing. He reveals the binding can be unmade at the coronation rite, when the veil between crown and wearer thins. Betrayal: Sera's exile was engineered by the crown-thing to bait exactly this. Emotional beat: horror, compassion, and the weight of choice.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Crowning
chapters.summary: POV Tam and Sera alternate. The trio prepares: Tam rallies old guard loyalists, Sera works counter-rites, and Odile confronts the truth Merric's map hid — the valley was founded to conceal the last swordspeaker line, her line. Her whole life was a hiding place. Emotional beat: grief for a stolen history, then fierce acceptance of the family beside her.

chapters.title: Coronation of the Devoured
chapters.summary: POV Odile. At the rite, the crown-thing moves to complete its possession through the new heir. Battle erupts in the cathedral; Tam holds the doors, Sera unravels the wards. Odile reaches the dais and, instead of striking, speaks her true name through the sword — unbinding king and creature alike as the oaths answer her at last. Emotional beat: climax; sacrifice offered and transformed.

chapters.title: A Home, Not a Hiding Place
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The freed king, diminished and grateful, offers her a place of honor; the valley elders offer restoration of her stolen legacy. She refuses both. With Sera and Tam, she returns to the valley not to hide but to open it — building a refuge for others the old world discarded. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging; identity chosen, not assigned.
